The Linker Standard

An engineered BESS package is more than battery cells.

Commercial and utility storage require alignment across PCS architecture, thermal control, grid compliance files, and commercial terms. Here is how Linker supports every project.

BESS ARCHITECTURE // SYSTEM SIZING
LINKER STANDARD 01

Build around documented electrical interfaces.

A commercial storage installation is defined by how the PCS, battery stack, BMS, and control components interact under real operating conditions.

Operating voltage windows, continuous C-rates, peak load limits, and thermal cooling methods all dictate how the system performs on site.

Linker supplies the hardware options with the electrical and control interface data from their datasheets and manuals on file, so your engineers can check that the interfaces align before equipment ships.

  • Sized for commercial load profiles, peak demands, and duty cycles.
  • PCS and BMS interface data on file for your matching.
  • Air-cooled and liquid-cooled options listed with their footprint data.
Project View: System Architecture · Component Matching · Technical Specifications

LINKER STANDARD 02

Technical documentation beside the hardware.

Interconnection reviews require the exact files. Grid operators and planning authorities need verified certificates and clear interface parameters.

Linker supplies the datasheets, manuals and compatibility lists on file with your equipment package, and requests the certificates and interface documents your grid operator asks for, project by project.

  • Unit certificates (VDE-AR-N 4110 / 4120 / Einheitenzertifikate), requested per project.
  • Modbus register maps, CAN protocols, and plant-controller interface notes, requested per project.
  • Datasheets and manuals with wiring diagrams, from the documents on file.

EPC DECISION FAQ

Technical and commercial questions from EPC teams.

Clear answers regarding project boundaries, early-stage collaboration, auxiliary systems, and grid alignment.

How early does Linker engage in the project lifecycle, and how do you support during the EPC bidding phase?

Linker enters during the early concept and tender phase. Before any purchase commitment, your proposal engineers share the project's single-line diagram, site constraints, and utility connection terms. Linker provides the platform options on file, indicative equipment footprints, preliminary auxiliary load data, and a bid-ready bill of materials for the topology your team specifies. The configuration stays flexible until the order is released.

How is auxiliary power for cooling, controls, and fire suppression handled within the system design?

Auxiliary loads for cooling, BMS, heating, and safety systems are documented per system. Feeding follows the site's auxiliary layout: typically an external site board, with a UPS for controls and safety circuits where the project requires it.

What data is provided to assist with medium-voltage protection settings and short-circuit calculations?

Inverter-based battery systems contribute limited fault current compared with synchronous machines. Linker requests the fault-current and protection data for your project, so your electrical engineers can size switchgear and set overcurrent, earth-fault, and differential relays.

How do container safety features, deflagration venting, and separation distances affect civil layout?

Container systems include documented clearance zones for maintenance access and air intake and exhaust. Linker requests the footprint drawings with the required safety buffers for your project, so civil planners can place transformers, roads, and neighboring enclosures.

How does Linker coordinate with the EPC's multidisciplinary team during detailed engineering and construction?

Linker's technical desk works with your electrical, civil, and automation engineers during detailed design. Linker provides foundation load points and clearances to structural engineers, terminal and cable data to the electrical team, and protocol maps to SCADA integrators, from the documents on file or requested for the project. If site conditions change before the order is released to production, the configuration can still be changed.
